stem:
The diagram shows six congruent equilateral triangles meeting at a common point.

Why can they be assembled to form a regular hexagon?

options.text: Each triangle angle is $60^{\circ}$, six of them make $360^{\circ}$ at the centre, and the outer sides are equal.
A regular hexagon is simply the label for any figure built from triangles.
Any six triangles around a point form a regular hexagon.
The same assembly also builds a regular pentagon from five equilateral triangles.

teacher.key_rationale: Six 60° angles fill 360° around a point; congruent equilateral triangles give equal outer sides and equal hexagon angles. B renames without the angle reason. C drops congruence and equilateral. D extends the rule to a pentagon, where five 60° angles do not fill 360°.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source tikz to six equilateral triangles around a point forming a regular hexagon.
